additional_requirements: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
examples: Swallowing food without chewing it properly.
Eating continuously and rapidly to the point where it is difficult to breathe.
Eating so urgently that there is no time to taste the food.
Eating at a speed that surprises others.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
examples: Eating until the stomach feels distended to the point of bursting and pain.
Eating so much that it is difficult to even stand up or move.
Continuing to eat until feeling nauseous or like vomiting.
Unable to stop eating even though it is physically uncomfortable and painful.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
examples: Feeling unbearable disgust and self-loathing after binging.
Falling into extreme depression and self-criticism immediately after binging.
Feeling intense guilt and regret over the fact that I binged again.
Feeling shame that I am pathetic and have weak willpower after binging.

patient_info.stressor_event: Major change in the number of arguments with spouse (e.g., either a lot more or a lot less than usual regarding child rearing, personal habits)
patient_info.stressor: As Patricia’s agency took on a high-visibility AR/VR campaign, the tension at home shifted sharply: she and her spouse began arguing far more often about her late nights, weekend networking events, and the way work kept spilling into their shared time. Over the next three months, she increasingly stayed up after arguments with leftover dinner-party food or delivery orders, and the eating episodes became more defined by unusually large amounts consumed quickly, a feeling that she could not rein herself in, and physical discomfort afterward. Her usual self-improvement mindset turned punitive as she felt guilty and disgusted after these episodes, especially when they followed evenings that were supposed to include yoga, running, or creative work. She first sought help through her company’s employee assistance program after realizing the pattern was no longer just “stress snacking,” and was referred for psychiatric evaluation.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: I came in because after everyone goes to bed, I’ll tell myself I’m just having some leftovers, and then I realize I’ve eaten half a tray of catered pasta, the dessert from a client dinner, and whatever snacks were in the pantry in one sitting.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I start, especially after a tense night with my husband, it feels like the decision-making part of me goes offline and I keep reaching for more even while I’m thinking, ‘Patricia, stop, this is enough.’

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
S051.manifestation: I eat so fast standing at the kitchen island or scrolling through work emails that I barely taste it, and sometimes I look down and the containers are empty before I’ve really registered what I was eating.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
S052.manifestation: By the end I’m often so full that my waistband hurts and I have to sit upright on the couch for a while because lying down makes me feel sick.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
S055.manifestation: Afterward I feel embarrassed and disgusted with myself, like I’ve blown the whole disciplined person I try to be, and I’ll sit there thinking I should have gone for a run or done yoga instead.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.description: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: For the last three months, there’s been at least one night almost every week where I end up eating like this after an argument or a late work event, and some weeks it happens twice.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I’m still keeping up with work, but the mornings after these nights I feel drained and ashamed, and I’ve started skipping plans like yoga or creative time because I don’t want to face anyone.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This pattern really started when the AR/VR campaign ramped up and the arguments at home got worse, about three months ago.
